root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Accepted: Kaulich Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 c5

overview: In the accepted BDG Black strikes at the d4 pawn with 5...c5, giving back the extra pawn at times, and aims for a healthy centre. White has two pawns' worth of play for the missing e- and f-pawns and normally plays 6.Bc4 or Bg5 with quick development. Theory judges Black fine if accurate.

white_ideas.idea: Use the open e- and f-files with Bc4, Bg5 and Qe2
Attack on the kingside before Black consolidates

black_ideas.idea: Strike at d4 with ...c5, develop ...e6 and ...Nc6
Return the pawn for safety if needed

typical_structures.structure: Open e-file with White ahead in development
Black pawn on c5 against d4

character.notes: White offers a pawn and Black can hit the centre, so the play is forcing and tactical.

gambit.notes: White is a pawn down after 4...exf3 5.Nxf3 and Black can keep it with careful play.

soundness.notes: Often viewed as dubious at top level because Black can consolidate; club results are better.

structure.notes: Open with active pieces and files.

approach.notes: The BDG is played by few strong players, so offbeat.

level.notes: Needs known tactics and also understanding of the open lines.

sublines_that_differ.name: Other 5th
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 Bg4
sublines_that_differ.how: A different Black try with no c5.

character.reason: A pawn down for a lead in development, with open lines and mutual threats.

gambit.reason: White gives the e-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Most strong players consider the BDG unsound at the top.

structure.reason: The e-file and diagonals open after the exchanges.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play the BDG.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never Beginner and Black's reply wants known lines.

plans.reason: White's compensation is time and pressure on the kingside.
